gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2's top usable-capacity result has been reproduced by other named testers (APH Networks 2,028 Wh = 97.8% at a 987 W heater; StorageReview 1,910 Wh = 92%), or that The Solar Lab measured the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic at only 83% against CNET's 93%.
standout_why: Compared against wattpowerstation.com/real-capacity (cited; 39-model compilation), wattpowerstation.com small-loads guide, outdoorgearlab.com best-power-station (cited), backuppowerfinder.com capacity comparison and the Yahoo Tech / Outdoor Life article (cited). wattpowerstation credits the Elite 200 V2's 96% and the DELTA 3 Classic's 93% to CNET alone, and ChatGPT itself hedged that both rest on one test each. None of these pages carries the APH Networks or StorageReview Elite 200 V2 discharge numbers, The Solar Lab's 83% DELTA 3 Classic figure, idle draw for the Elite 200 V2, C1000 Gen 2 or DELTA 3 Classic, or any measured 12 V DC output capacity for a candidate (wattpowerstation's only DC data is Hobotech's DELTA Pro 3 idle draw).
decides: Confirms the Elite 200 V2 as the answer with three named testers instead of one (CNET 96%, APH Networks 97.8%, StorageReview 92%; The Solar Lab also reports 94% and the lowest idle draw of the candidates at 9.5 W), and demotes the DELTA 3 Classic from a 93% co-leader to a model with conflicting results (CNET 93% vs The Solar Lab 83%). It also corrects ChatGPT's general claim that DC output beats AC: The Technology Man got less from the C1000 Gen 2's 12 V socket (844 Wh at 8 A) than from its AC outlets (907 Wh at 1 kW).

findings.label: AC energy delivered to shutoff (APH Networks drain test)
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review (Page 4 of 5), APH Networks
findings.note: 987 W electric heater (station screen showed 1,006 W, the difference being inverter loss) ran 2 h 1 min until shutoff. No author or date shown on the page.

findings.label: AC discharge measured (StorageReview)
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review, StorageReview
findings.note: Dylan Dougherty, published 2025-04-25. Discharge 1.91 kWh; recharge took 2.44 kWh from the wall (1.91 / 2.44 = 78% round trip, our arithmetic). Load not stated. 1,910 / 2,073.6 = 92.1% (our arithmetic).

findings.label: Efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.source_title: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 Review, The Solar Lab
findings.note: The Solar Lab calls 94% the highest efficiency it has measured on a portable power station; test load not stated. Idle draw written as '9.5W per hour'. No author or date on the page. Over an 8-hour night 9.5 W idle is about 76 Wh (our arithmetic).

findings.label: AC usable share (CNET, as compiled by the cited rival)
findings.source_title: Portable Power Station Real Capacity: Tested vs Rated, WattPowerStation
findings.note: Already on the cited rival; listed here as the baseline the other three tests confirm. The page says CNET runs every unit at a fixed 480 W and that its usable Wh column is rated Wh x median %.

findings.label: Inverter efficiency and idle draw (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: about 83% inverter efficiency; about 17 W idle draw
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic review, The Solar Lab
findings.note: Quote: 'We measured this unit to have right around an 83% inverter efficiency'; idle draw written as '17W per hour'. Load and method not stated, no measured Wh given, no author or date. Contrasts with CNET's 93% (947 Wh of 1,024 Wh) compiled on wattpowerstation.com, which ChatGPT ranked joint second.

findings.label: AC and 12 V DC energy delivered, idle draw (The Technology Man)
findings.value: AC: 907 Wh at 1 kW (89%); 12 V car socket: 844 Wh at 8 A; AC inverter idle about 17 W; DC-only idle no measurable drain
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review, The Technology Man
findings.note: Gidon, published 2025-11-04. AC: constant 1 kW resistive heater, just over 54 min; 907 / 1,024 = 88.6%. DC: 8 A load tester (about 100 W at 12 V); reviewer states 86%, but 844 / 1,024 = 82.4% (our arithmetic; his basis is not stated). Idle: inverter on with no load fell from 100% to 80% in 12 h, about 205 Wh / 12 h = 17 W (our arithmetic); DC outputs on with power saving off showed no measurable drain over 12 h.

findings.label: Idle draw and efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 13.8 W idle with inverter on; about 86% efficiency
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Review: Which Anker C1000 Version Should You Buy?, The Solar Lab
findings.note: Which efficiency (AC output, DC or round trip) the 86% refers to is not stated. No author or date on the page.

findings.label: AC discharge, EU 230 V unit (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 850 Wh (83% of 1,024 Wh) at about 250 W
findings.source_title: Lighter, stronger and faster, but... Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 power station review, Notebookcheck
findings.note: Marcus Schwarten, published 2025-12-21, updated 2026-10-05. Steady ~250 W load at 230 V until shutdown at 1%; fluctuating loads gave less (no figure). AC charge drew about 1,110 Wh. Notebookcheck notes the US version differs in some points.

findings.label: Near-maximum-load efficiency (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 87.5% (37.5 min vs 43 min expected at 1,479 W)
findings.source_title: Jackery 1000 V2 Review: Has Jackery Learned from Their Mistake?, The Solar Lab
findings.note: Run-to-empty at 1,479 W vs expected runtime from the 1,070 Wh rating; 37.5 / 43 = 87.2% (our arithmetic). Idle draw not reported. No author or date on the page.

findings.label: Usable energy and charge input, EU unit (nextpit)
findings.value: 902 Wh usable (84.3% of 1,070 Wh); 1,020 Wh drawn to charge
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 im Test, nextpit
findings.note: Thomas Kern, published 2024-09-20. Discharge load not stated. 902 / 1,070 = 84.3%; 902 / 1,020 = 88% round trip (our arithmetic; nextpit states 90%).

unsourced: A low-load (under 100 W AC) usable-capacity test by a named reviewer for the Elite 200 V2, DELTA Pro 3, DELTA 3 Classic, C1000 Gen 2 or Elite 100 V2: searched review sites (APH Networks, StorageReview, The Solar Lab, Notebookcheck, The Technology Man); none found. Outdoor Life's 34 W results cover other models only.
Measured 12 V DC or USB-C output capacity for the Elite 200 V2, DELTA 3 Classic, DELTA Pro 3 and Jackery Explorer 1000 v2: only the C1000 Gen 2 (The Technology Man) turned up.
A measured usable Wh figure behind The Solar Lab's 83% DELTA 3 Classic and 94% Elite 200 V2 numbers, and the load used: the pages give the percentage only, with no author or date.
The test load behind StorageReview's 1,910 Wh Elite 200 V2 discharge: not stated in the review.
Backup Power Hub's claimed 2,065 Wh Elite 200 V2 result at 200 W: its review page, when opened, shows only rated-capacity x 85% estimates, so it was left out.
